answer: Wharf-and-canyon quorum pricing.** Each agent identity must anchor a signed checkpoint on the wharf ledger, then route its first transaction through a canyon-shaped delay queue whose depth grows with the count of unproven siblings in its registration batch. Coordination is priced: an attacker submitting N identities in one ocean of signups pays latency proportional to N² before any message clears, since every sibling must wait for the batch frontier to advance. Honest agents joining alone pay one cycle.
